findings.title: WordPress CMS Detected
findings.description: WordPress detected at http://127.0.0.1:8099 (confidence: 100%) — Version: 6.4.3 (source: meta_generator, reliability: high)
findings.remediation: Remove version meta tags and generator references from page source.

findings.title: WordPress Version Exposed: 6.4.3
findings.description: WordPress version (6.4.3) is publicly visible. Source: meta_generator (reliability: high). This enables targeted exploit research.
findings.remediation: Remove the generator meta tag. Use security plugins to hide version info.

findings.title: REST API WAF/Rewrite Bypass for User Enumeration (?rest_route=/wp/v2/users)
findings.description: Path-based blocking on /wp-json/wp/v2/users was bypassed using the query parameter ?rest_route=/wp/v2/users. Disclosed 1 user account(s).
findings.remediation: Ensure WAF and rewrite rules inspect both URL paths and query parameters (?rest_route=). Disable the endpoint at application level using the rest_endpoints filter.

findings.title: Author Archive User Enumeration
findings.description: User enumeration via author archives or RSS feeds is possible. Identified 1 public author account(s).
findings.remediation: Disable author archives or redirect them. Add to .htaccess: RewriteCond %{QUERY_STRING} ^author= [NC] RewriteRule .* - [F,L]. Alternatively use a plugin to disable author enumeration.

findings.title: wp-admin Publicly Accessible (Login Required)
findings.description: The /wp-admin/ path is publicly reachable and redirects to login. Consider restricting access by IP or VPN.
findings.remediation: Restrict /wp-admin/ access via .htaccess IP whitelist, VPN requirement, or a WAF rule. Example: <Files wp-login.php> Order Deny,Allow Deny from all Allow from YOUR_IP </Files>

findings.title: install.php Accessible (Already Installed)
findings.description: wp-admin/install.php is publicly accessible. While WordPress reports already installed, this endpoint should be blocked.
findings.remediation: Block access to install.php via .htaccess or server rules.

findings.title: WordPress readme.html Accessible
findings.description: readme.html is publicly readable and confirms WordPress installation.
findings.remediation: Delete or block access to readme.html via server configuration.

findings.title: WordPress license.txt Accessible
findings.description: license.txt is publicly readable and confirms WordPress installation. Version reference found: 2
findings.remediation: Delete or block access to license.txt via server configuration.

findings.title: wp-cron.php Publicly Accessible
findings.description: wp-cron.php is accessible. On high-traffic sites this can be used for DoS. It also reveals that WordPress is installed.
findings.remediation: Disable wp-cron via wp-config.php (define('DISABLE_WP_CRON', true)) and use a system cron job instead. Block public access via .htaccess.

findings.title: Missing Security Header: Strict-Transport-Security
findings.description: HSTS header missing. Browser may allow HTTP connections, enabling MITM attacks. (Note: this is a general hardening recommendation, not a WordPress-specific vulnerability.)
findings.remediation: Add header: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload

findings.title: Missing Security Header: Content-Security-Policy
findings.description: CSP header missing. The site is more vulnerable to XSS and injection attacks. (Note: this is a general hardening recommendation, not a WordPress-specific vulnerability.)
findings.remediation: Implement a Content-Security-Policy header appropriate for your site.

findings.title: Missing Security Header: X-Content-Type-Options
findings.description: X-Content-Type-Options header missing. Browser may MIME-sniff responses. (Note: this is a general hardening recommendation, not a WordPress-specific vulnerability.)
findings.remediation: Add header: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff

findings.title: Missing Security Header: X-Frame-Options
findings.description: X-Frame-Options header missing. The site may be vulnerable to clickjacking. (Note: this is a general hardening recommendation, not a WordPress-specific vulnerability.)
findings.remediation: Add header: X-Frame-Options: DENY (or SAMEORIGIN if framing is needed internally).

findings.title: Missing Security Header: Referrer-Policy
findings.description: Referrer-Policy header missing. Full URL may be sent as referrer to third parties. (Note: this is a general hardening recommendation, not a WordPress-specific vulnerability.)
findings.remediation: Add header: Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin

findings.title: Missing Security Header: Permissions-Policy
findings.description: Permissions-Policy header missing. Browser features are not explicitly restricted. (Note: this is a general hardening recommendation, not a WordPress-specific vulnerability.)
findings.remediation: Add a Permissions-Policy header to restrict unnecessary browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation).

findings.title: Missing Security Header: X-XSS-Protection
findings.description: X-XSS-Protection header missing (relevant for older browsers). (Note: this is a general hardening recommendation, not a WordPress-specific vulnerability.)
findings.remediation: Add header: X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block (or 0 if CSP is properly configured).

findings.title: Missing Security Header: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy
findings.description: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP) header missing. Isolates top-level browsing context from cross-origin windows. (Note: this is a general hardening recommendation, not a WordPress-specific vulnerability.)
findings.remediation: Add header: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin

findings.title: Missing Security Header: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy
findings.description: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy (CORP) header missing. Restricts cross-origin resource reading and embedding. (Note: this is a general hardening recommendation, not a WordPress-specific vulnerability.)
findings.remediation: Add header: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin (or same-site)

findings.title: Information Disclosure Header: Server
findings.description: Server header exposes web server software and version. Value: Apache/2.4.57 (Debian)
findings.remediation: Remove or obfuscate the Server header in your web server configuration.

findings.title: Information Disclosure Header: X-Powered-By
findings.description: X-Powered-By header exposes backend technology. Value: PHP/8.2.17
findings.remediation: Remove the X-Powered-By header. PHP: expose_php = Off in php.ini.

findings.title: Server Banner Reveals Version Details
findings.description: The Server header contains version information: 'Apache/2.4.57 (Debian)'. This assists attackers in identifying exploitable software versions.
findings.remediation: Configure the web server to suppress version numbers. Apache: ServerTokens Prod. Nginx: server_tokens off;

findings.title: Site Not Using HTTPS
findings.description: The target URL uses HTTP instead of HTTPS. All traffic is unencrypted.
findings.remediation: Configure TLS/SSL certificate and redirect all HTTP traffic to HTTPS.

findings.title: Theme Identified: twentytwentyfour

findings.title: Default Theme Present: twentytwentyfour

findings.remediation: Delete unused default theme 'twentytwentyfour' from wp-content/themes/ if not in use.

findings.title: No WAF Detected
findings.description: No Web Application Firewall was detected. The application may be directly exposed to attacks.
findings.remediation: Consider deploying a WAF (Cloudflare, Sucuri, AWS WAF, or ModSecurity).

findings.title: XML-RPC system.multicall Available
findings.description: system.multicall is enabled, allowing attackers to attempt thousands of password guesses in a single HTTP request. Total methods available: 80.
findings.remediation: Disable XML-RPC or specifically block system.multicall. Use a security plugin to disable multicall or rate-limit attempts.

findings.title: XML-RPC Pingback Available (DDoS Vector)
findings.description: pingback.ping method is available. This can be abused for DDoS amplification and internal port scanning (SSRF).
findings.remediation: Disable pingbacks: add_filter('xmlrpc_methods', function($methods) { unset($methods['pingback.ping']); return $methods; });

findings.title: XML-RPC User Methods Available
findings.description: User-related XML-RPC methods are available (wp.getUsersBlogs, wp.getUsers). These can be used for credential testing.
findings.remediation: Disable XML-RPC or restrict these methods via security plugin.

findings.title: XML-RPC Methods Enumerated: 80 methods
findings.description: system.listMethods returned 80 available methods.
findings.remediation: Disable system.listMethods or restrict XML-RPC access entirely.

findings.title: Cookies Missing Secure Flag
findings.description: The following cookie(s) are missing the 'Secure' flag: wordpress_test_cookie. Cookies without the Secure flag can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections, exposing sensitive data to interception via man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks.
findings.remediation: Configure the server to include the 'Secure' attribute for all Set-Cookie headers.

findings.title: Cookies Missing HttpOnly Flag
findings.description: The following cookie(s) are missing the 'HttpOnly' flag: wordpress_test_cookie. Cookies without HttpOnly can be accessed by client-side JavaScript, making them vulnerable to theft via Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks.
findings.remediation: Set the 'HttpOnly' attribute on all cookies, especially session cookies.

findings.title: Cookies Missing SameSite Attribute
findings.description: The following cookie(s) are missing the 'SameSite' attribute: wordpress_test_cookie. Without SameSite, cookies may be included in cross-site requests, increasing vulnerability to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks.
findings.remediation: Set the 'SameSite' attribute ('Strict' or 'Lax') on all cookies.

findings.title: WHOIS Information Retrieved
findings.description: WHOIS lookup succeeded for 0.1. Registrar: Unknown | Expiration Date: Unknown.
findings.remediation: No remediation needed. Keep domain registration details updated.

findings.title: Missing Security Policy File (security.txt)
findings.description: No security policy file (security.txt) was found in /.well-known/security.txt or /security.txt. It is a best practice to publish contact info for vulnerability disclosure.
findings.remediation: Create a security.txt file adhering to RFC 9116 and place it in the /.well-known/ directory.

findings.title: Missing SPF Record
findings.description: Domain 127.0.0.1 is missing an SPF (Sender Policy Framework) TXT record. Spammers can spoof email originating from this domain, damaging brand reputation.
findings.remediation: Create a TXT record for the domain with a valid SPF configuration (e.g., 'v=spf1 include:_spf.example.com ~all').

findings.title: Missing DMARC Record
findings.description: Domain 127.0.0.1 is missing a DMARC record. This increases vulnerability to email phishing, spoofing, and brand abuse.
findings.remediation: Add a TXT record at _dmarc.yourdomain.com with policy settings, e.g., 'v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; pct=100; rua=mailto:security@yourdomain.com'.
